issues.legal_issue: A decree-created charge does not make a debt secured for purposes of post-decree debt reduction when the debt was unsecured when the suit was filed.
material_facts: The suit was based on a promissory note, and the debt was unsecured when the suit was filed.
The decree later created a charge over the debtor’s property.
After default, the debtor applied during execution for reduction of the decretal amount.
issues.conclusion: The post-decree reduction provision did not apply because the debt was unsecured when the suit was filed; the charge created by the decree did not change that result. The appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(m), 3 and 4 of the U.P. Zamindar’s Debt Reduction Act, 1953, read with section 100 of the Transfer of Property Act, whether a debt is secured is determined as of the date the suit was filed. A debt secured at that time by a mortgage or a charge within section 100 is a secured debt, and the decree in that suit relates to a secured debt. A charge created only by the decree does not convert a debt that was unsecured when the suit was filed into a secured debt for the purposes of section 4. The Court relied on the parallel wording and interpretation of sections 3 and 4; it cited no earlier cases.

predicates.post_decree_debt_reduction_proceeding: A party sought reduction of a debt under a post-decree procedure after a judgment had been entered.
predicates.debt_unsecured_when_suit_filed: The debt was not secured by a mortgage or qualifying charge when the underlying suit was filed.
predicates.decree_created_charge: The decree itself created a charge over property to secure payment of the debt.

issues.definition: When a party seeks post-decree debt reduction, the relief is unavailable if the debt was unsecured when the suit was filed, even if the decree later created a charge.
